speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; can you tell me if you have any family history of bleeding disorders or if you are currently taking any blood-thinning medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience bleeding from your gums when brushing your teeth or frequent nosebleeds? Given the family history of joint swelling, have you ever had bleeding into your joints or muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: PT, aPTT, Bleeding_Time, Platelet_Count
Do you recall if the bleeding after the extraction stopped completely and then restarted days later, or was it continuous from the moment the surgery ended?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT: 15 sec, aPTT: 60 sec, Bleeding Time: 6 min, Platelet Count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged aPTT with normal PT and platelet count, combined with your family history of joint swelling, strongly suggests Hemophilia A. To confirm this, I need to check your specific clotting factor levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII activity level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII is normal, let's check Factor IX levels to rule out Hemophilia B, which also presents with prolonged aPTT and joint bleeding. REQUEST TEST: Factor IX activity level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX are normal, let's check for a Factor XI deficiency, which can cause prolonged aPTT and bleeding after surgery. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI activity level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factors VIII, IX, and XI are normal, I need to check for Factor XII deficiency, which causes a prolonged aPTT but typically does not cause bleeding symptoms. REQUEST TEST: Factor XII activity level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since standard coagulation factors are normal, I suspect an issue with platelet function despite the normal platelet count and bleeding time. Have you ever experienced prolonged bleeding after other minor surgeries, cuts, or dental work in the past? REQUEST TEST: Platelet Aggregation Study

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal platelet aggregation and standard coagulation factors, I need to investigate von Willebrand disease, which can present with a prolonged aPTT due to low Factor VIII levels or functional defects. REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Ristocetin Cofactor Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prolonged aPTT with normal PT, platelet count, and all specific factor assays including vWF, I suspect a rare coagulation factor deficiency such as Factor X or a contact factor issue not yet ruled out by standard screens. DIAGNOSIS READY: Factor X Deficiency
